entries.title: Leviticus 14:2
segments: When any one has reason to believe that he is delivered from the reigning power of sin, he should make it known, and seek admission to the fellowship of the church.

entries.title: Leviticus 14:4
segments:
Scarlet; wool dyed red. 
 
  Hyssop; a bushy plant of a spicy, fragrant smell, much used in ceremonial cleansings.

entries.title: Leviticus 14:5
segments: Running water; living, fresh water, in distinction from that which is stagnant, or has been long standing.

entries.title: Leviticus 14:6
segments:
vv 6-7. 
 
  Shall dip them--shall sprinkle--shall let the living bird loose; the fragrant hyssop and cedar wood, the bright scarlet, and the running water, are all symbols of purity, as the blood is of cleansing.  The sprinkling of the man with these is a sign of his purification.  The living bird is first symbolically purified by being dipped in the blood and water, along with the hyssop, cedar wood, and scarlet.  Then it is let go free, to signify that the leper thus purified is set free and restored to the camp.  But he needs a further expiation before he can be restored to the privileges of the sanctuary, as the sacred writer proceeds to state.

entries.title: Leviticus 14:8
segments: He who is really cleansed from the pollution of sin, will gratefully acknowledge his indebtedness for the blessing to the grace of God in Jesus Christ, and will seek to purify himself more and more, and to perfect holiness in the fear of God.

entries.title: Leviticus 14:10
segments: Three tenth-deals; a tenth-deal, or an omer, is the tenth of an ephah.
One log; somewhat more than half a pint.

entries.title: Leviticus 14:11
segments: Maketh him clean; cleanses him ceremonially, as described in the following verses.

entries.title: Leviticus 14:12
segments: The change which has been wrought in a sinner when he becomes pious, is never to be ascribed to himself or to creatures, but always to God, and the glory to be given to Him.

entries.title: Leviticus 14:17
segments:
vv 17-18. 
 
  Ear--thumb--toe--head; in token that all his members and faculties need cleansing through the efficacy of the atonement, by the Holy Spirit; and should all be consecrated to the service of God.

entries.title: Leviticus 14:21
segments: Although a man who repents and forsakes his sins, is pardoned through faith in Christ, yet, to be saved, he must devote his powers of body and mind as an offering of gratitude to his service.

entries.title: Leviticus 14:32
segments: None are excluded from the benefits of Christ's salvation on account of their poverty; nor can any be saved except through faith in him, and consecration to his service and glory.

entries.title: Leviticus 14:37
segments:
If the plague be in the walls; this has been supposed to be something corrosive, which caused the walls to moulder away. 
 
  Lower than the wall; indentations or hollow places in the wall.

entries.title: Leviticus 14:44
segments: Fretting leprosy; eating away the walls, or causing them to decay.

entries.title: Leviticus 14:45
segments: Not only our souls, but our bodies, and all that we possess, are affected by sin.  Moth and rust corrupt; thieves break through and steal.  The earthly house of this tabernacle must be dissolved; the earth and all in it burnt up.  Happy they, and they only, who have a building of God, a house not made with hands, eternal in the heavens.

entries.title: Leviticus 14:53
segments: Let go the living bird; signifying that the house, thus purified, is free to the use of its owner.  See note on
